Splitting them also makes the new filter 3 checkable at a glance, because comparing the two lists shows the swap genuinely drops the dumbbell rather than reusing it. Bench went with them: it was a stale tag, since the execution never names a bench and a chest-supported row is not what the primary drill is. No change to focus, execution, swap, category, or role. || FILTER 3 / INVERSION FIX. The old swap was a chest-supported machine row plus a TRX Y-fly, tagged Machine and TRX, while the execution needs only a dumbbell and a band. Count was equal at two against two, so it slipped past the more-implements half of the check, but it inverted on scarcity: both swap implements must be booked, neither execution implement ever is. The fallback was the harder thing to get. Machine and TRX are gone. The new swap is bodyweight, so swap_equipment is omitted - nothing to reserve, nothing to tag. It still hits the same non-axial back focus, and it hits it from a genuinely different angle rather than repeating the primary: prone horizontal-plane retraction on the floor against a seated row plus a standing band pull. Floor work is a regression in load, which is the honest trade for a swap that must never need a booking.

The execution is a cable row; the swap was a Single-Arm Cable Row plus a press, also cable. AGENTS.md: 'The swap must use different equipment than the primary movement' and 'an athlete whose cable station is taken still cannot do it.' The swap is now a single Dumbbell: one implement against one, common-tier against reserved, so it passes the inversion check, and the diagonal sling pattern survives intact - single-arm row into an internal-rotation press is the same contralateral intent on a different implement.

name: Commercial Gym French Contrast
execution: Heavy Trap Bar Deadlift (85%) + Bench Altitude Drop
swap: Heavy Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift + Box Drop Jump

manual.why: TAG CLEANUP ONLY - the station-logistics problem is NOT fixed and is still queued. Dead 'Barbell' tag removed: no barbell is named in the execution or the swap, and since the whole point of this complex is that the trap bar is droppable, a stray barbell tag was actively misleading about the safe exit. Kettlebell is named only in the swap and moves to swap_equipment. STILL OPEN: this is a four-station complex whose swap adds a fifth implement, and the audit flagged the floor logistics as the worst in the database. || STRUCTURAL FIX - THE COMPLEX IS DEMOTED TO A GENUINE PAIR, NOT PATCHED. Audit reasoning, as recorded on id 130: 'this is a four-station complex whose swap adds a fifth implement, and the audit flagged the floor logistics as the worst in the database.' Fixing only the swap would have been treating the symptom. The root problem is structural: a complex in this database is a PAIR of movements - AGENTS.md defines it as 'paired movements, e.g. a brace + an explosive expression'. This record held four movements across four stations and six equipment types, so it could not satisfy filter 3 at any swap, because the violation was the shape of the record rather than its equipment list. What survives is the actual French contrast: heavy trap bar at 85% into a bench altitude drop, which is the real heavy-to-light contrast, drops onto two feet, and has a safe exit because a trap bar can be dropped. Two implements at two adjacent stations instead of four at six. What is lost is real and I will not pretend otherwise: the DB jump squat and band pogo are gone, so this is no longer the 'advanced rate of force development' tour de force it claimed to be. Swap is one dumbbell plus one box, two common-tier implements against two reserved ones, which passes the inversion check on both conditions. SEE THE REPORT: I also considered moving this to circuits.jsonl and recommend against it - the reasoning is in manual form in my report to the coach, not here.
manual.cue: Own the contrast, station to station.

name: Hinge Potentiation
execution: Heavy Trap Bar RDL (85% 1RM) + Explosive Broad Jump
swap: Heavy Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (Rear-Foot Elevated) + Vertical Jump (DBs Released at Hip)

manual.why: FILTER 3 INVERSION FIX. Original audit rationale not recorded, so re-derived, but again it is mechanical rather than a judgement call. equipment was tagged ['Trap Bar', 'Dumbbell', 'Kettlebell'] while only the Trap Bar appears in the execution - Dumbbell and Kettlebell are swap-only and were folded in. Split honestly, the inversion check fires immediately: the primary needs one implement, the swap needs a dumbbell AND a kettlebell, so the fallback is a two-station errand against a one-station default, and it asks for a second piece of kit precisely when the first is already unavailable. The swap is now a single Dumbbell doing both jobs - the RDL loads it and the jump releases it at the hip - so one common-tier implement against one reserved one, passing both conditions. Release at the hip rather than a full drop keeps a genuine safe exit and avoids the mid-complex drop that flagged id 123. Primary untouched: trap bar is droppable, the broad jump lands on two feet, and hip hinge into horizontal take-off is one continuous direction.
